prompt: Interrupts start enabled (IF = 1). The code takes `outer = irq_save()`, then `inner = irq_save()`, then calls `irq_restore(inner)` and finally `irq_restore(outer)`. `irq_restore` runs `sti` only if IF was set in the saved flags. What is IF after each step?

trace.label: [IF] after `outer = irq_save()` (outer holds the old flags)
[IF bit in `inner`] the flags captured by the second `irq_save()`
[IF] after a naive version where each section is `cli(); ...; sti();` and the inner `sti` has run

explain: irq_save reads RFLAGS (IF is bit 9, 0x200) and then clears IF. The outer call captures IF = 1; the inner call captures IF = 0 because interrupts are already off, so restoring it does not run `sti` and the outer critical section stays protected. Only the outer restore turns interrupts back on. The naive cli/sti pair re-enables interrupts too early when the inner section ends, leaving the rest of the outer section exposed to the handler. `lock xadd` leaves the old value in the register, so atomic_add returns 10 and memory becomes 15.
